observation: In multi-parent dynamic decomposition, selectTargetParent previously allowed any receipt carrying a matching targetRef+clauseRef to influence target multiplicity before checking organ, completion status, provenance, or authorized triage classification. An irrelevant, incomplete, or non-GUT receipt aimed at a second contested parent could therefore convert an otherwise valid single-parent decomposition into multiple-contested-parents-targeted HOLD.
risk: A non-qualifying receipt could alter routing behavior without being admissible metabolic evidence, creating a denial-of-metabolism / false ambiguity path and violating the rule that only qualified evidence may regulate downstream organ behavior.
resolution: VAJRA dynamic decomposition v1.1 now makes multi-parent target selection depend on qualifyTriageReceipt. Only completed GUT receipts with matching targetRef+clauseRef, non-empty provenance, and an authorized contamination classification can establish parent targeting or target multiplicity. Non-qualifying receipts remain auditable later in the parent-scoped pass but cannot manufacture multi-parent ambiguity.
boundary: This resolves only routing influence from non-qualifying receipts. It does not establish source truth, prove provenance independence, execute generated facets, admit a capability into persistent body state, or authorize self-modification.
